title: Clear a carton jammed askew where the conveyor guides narrow
instruction: Clear the jammed carton: push it through the guides and out of their far end.
context: Conveyor operators and material handlers (O*NET 53-7011.00, 53-7062.00) clear cartons that turn askew and catch at a guide joint. A forced carton crushes or stops the line. Unlike TK-RWRT5A (a gripped beam squared by pulling a named end, method given), this carton is too wide to grip, starts jammed, must be cleared by pushing alone, flat on the lane, and no method is given.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases on the table top: x away from the arms, y to the robot's left, heights above the table. Lane: centre line along x at y -12.0 (in front of the right arm), on the bare table. Guides (fixed, unpainted steel bars, 4.0 cm tall, standing on the table along x): before the shoulder, two bars 18.0 cm long (x 16.0 to 34.0) and 1.2 cm thick, inner faces at y -6.1 and -17.9 (11.8 cm apart); past the shoulder, two bars painted safety yellow 6.0 cm long (x 34.0 to 40.0) and 1.8 cm thick, sharing the same outer faces (y -4.9 and -19.1), inner faces at y -6.7 and -17.3 (10.6 cm apart). So at x 34.0 each guide steps 6 mm in at a square shoulder with no lead-in, and the lane is open at both ends (x 16.0 and x 40.0). Carton (loose, dark brown corrugated cardboard box): 12.0 cm long, 10.0 cm wide, 5.0 cm tall, 300 g, flat on the table, its centre at x 28.8, y -12.0, turned 9 degrees counter-clockwise seen from above. Its corners are then at (x, y): front-left (34.0, -6.1), front-right (35.5, -16.0), rear-left (22.1, -8.0), rear-right (23.7, -17.9): the front-left corner is touching the left shoulder face and the left guide, the rear-right corner touches the right guide, and the front-right corner is already 1.5 cm into the narrow part. It is too wide to grip either way (the gripper opens 9.4 cm). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The carton must go through the lane, flat on the table, never around or over the guides. Measured with a ruler from the guides' near end (x 16.0), shoulders (x 34.0) and far end (x 40.0), with a photo from above and the video. Flat: top within 5 degrees of level, underside on the table (within 1 mm). Let go: no part of either gripper within 5 mm of the carton. Score 1.0: every part of the carton beyond the far end (x 40.0 or more), its centre within 6 cm of the lane's centre line (y -12.0), flat, still (under 1 cm/s) and let go. Score 0.5: in the narrow part, square to the lane within 3 degrees, leading edge at least 3.0 cm past the shoulders and some of it still before the far end, flat, still and let go. Score 0 for the whole trial if at any moment the carton's near end goes back past the guides' near end (below x 16.0), any part of it is beyond a guide's outer face (y -4.9 or -19.1) between x 16.0 and 40.0, or, while any part of it is between x 16.0 and 40.0, it is not flat on the lane (so lifting or tipping it over the shoulders earns nothing). Score 0 in every other case: still caught, backed off but not fed in, tipped, off the table, moving, or touched by a gripper. The trial ends at 1.0 once that has held for 1 s; otherwise the last step is scored.
reset_notes: 1. Leave the four guide bars where they are (fixed). 2. Stand the carton flat on the table on one of its 12 by 10 cm faces (5 cm tall), in the lane between the steel guides. 3. Turn it 9 degrees counter-clockwise seen from above. 4. Slide it forward until its front-left corner touches both the left yellow shoulder face (x 34.0) and the left steel guide (y -6.1), at (34.0, -6.1). 5. Check its rear-right corner touches the right steel guide at (23.7, -17.9) and its front-right corner is at (35.5, -16.0), 1.5 cm into the narrow part. 6. Move both arms to their home poses, clear of the carton. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. Rigid boxes with one high friction for every contact (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic); real cartons crush at a corner. The conveyor is the bare table, with no rollers or belt. The 6 mm step stands for a misaligned joint between two guide sections, where the downstream section is set narrower with no lead-in. The layout is fixed, so a memorised replay of the demo cannot be ruled out; general habits fail (README).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (re-scored from its video under the revised scorer); demo: 1.0 (re-run under the revised scorer)
